## The Census Bureau

::: r-fit-text
Constitution requires a headcount of *all persons* every 10 years

First purpose: Apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives

- 1790: First national count — just six questions

- 1902: Congress establishes a permanent agency

- 2026: Bureau lives within the Department of Commerce

Sometimes mundane, sometimes controversial!

- Slavery, citizenship, genealogy

- Indigenous Peoples and LGBTQ+ civil rights

- Equitable representation and gerrymandering\
:::

## Diverse Data, Many Purposes

::: r-fit-text
Today, the Census Bureau conducts over 130 different surveys.

Each data product has its own life cycle and its own peculiar characteristics.

- **Decennial Census of Population and Housing (10-Year).** As required by US constitution, used for redistricting and apportionment

- **American Community Survey (Annual).** The social and economic needs of communities, across many demographic characteristics.

- **Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (Annual).** Income and poverty statistics for all school districts, counties, and states.

- **Current Population Survey (Monthly).** How we work — types of jobs held, wages, hours worked.

Census data is used to distribute **more than \$675 billion** in federal funds to local, state, and tribal governments each year.
:::

::: notes
- **Economic Census (5-Year).** Businesses & economy at national, state, and local levels.

- **Census of Governments (3-Year).** State/local government employment and finances.

- **Small Area Health Insurance Estimates.**

Plus, States and communities use census data to allocate funding for neighborhood improvements, public health, education, transportation, and more.

Sources: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/sis/about/students101.html

TRANSITION: LOTS of data! Can be pretty overwhelming

<!-- By default a revealjs slide is 1050px wide by 700px tall. -->
:::

## Geographies Start with Blocks

[![Census geographies are built from Blocks, aggregated to Counties to States](/images/census-work/census-geo-levels.jpg){fig-alt="Hierarchy of US Census geographies, with Nation at the top and Blocks at the very bottom" fig-align="center" width="757"}](https://www2.census.gov/geo/pdfs/reference/geodiagram.pdf)

## Block Groups and Tracts

::: r-fit-text
[Geographies for BR Central](https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/onelineaddress?address=4450%20Harrisburg%20Blvd%2C%20Houston%2C%20Texas&benchmark=4&vintage=4)
**GEOID:** Unique ID or "name" for each census block. **48 201 310400 3032**

**FIPS:** Five-digit code for each unique state (**48**) and county (**201**).

**Tract:** Ideally contain about 4,000 people and 1,600 housing units. **310400**

**Block Group:** A subdivision of a census tract; generally contain between 600 and 3,000 people and 240 and 1,200 housing units. The smallest unit for which the Bureau tabulates data for *any other survey*. **Block Groups 1, 2, and 3**

**Block:** The smallest geographic unit for which the Bureau tabulates *decennial* census data. In cities, many blocks correspond to individual city blocks bounded by streets. **Block 3032**

Source: [Glossary at Census.gov](https://www.census.gov/glossary/)
:::

## Open Your Program

```{r}
#| label: install.library
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false
# Do this first
# install.packages(c("tidycensus", "mapview", "tidygeocoder", "ipumsr", "censusapi", "tidyverse"))

# Run this instead every time afterwards
my_packages <- c("tidycensus", "mapview", "tidygeocoder", "ipumsr", "censusapi", "tidyverse")
lapply(my_packages, library, character.only = TRUE)
```

### Set Up Census API Key

```{r}
#| label: check.api.key
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true
# Check to see if you already have a CENSUS_KEY or CENSUS_API_KEY saved
# If so, no further action is needed
get_api_key()
```

```{r}
#| label: set.api.key
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false
# If not, add your key to your Renviron file
census_api_key("PASTEYOURKEYHERE", overwrite = FALSE, install = TRUE)

# Reload .Renviron the first time
readRenviron("~/.Renviron")

# Confirm that the expected key is output in your R console
get_api_key()
```

## Harris County / Decennial

```{r}
#| label: load.vars
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true
#| output-location: slide

# From the tidycensus package:
# Demographic and Housing Characteristics File ("Decennial Census")
vars_dhc = load_variables(2020, dataset = "dhc")
View(vars_dhc)
```

```{r}
#| label: harris.blocks
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true
#| output-location: slide

harris_blocks = get_decennial(
  geography = "block group", 
  variables = "P1_001N", # TOTAL POPULATION
  state = "TX",
  county = "Harris County",
  sumfile = "dhc",
  year = 2020,
  geometry = FALSE, 
  show_call = TRUE
)

View(harris_blocks)
```
